thesis: A cheap, improvised rooftop refuge at night where somebody has been watching live television above the generated city. It feels lonely, comforting, inhabited, technically plausible, and a little impossible because a giant glowing vacuum-tube monument occupies the nearby skyline.

mustAlwaysFeelLike: a private refuge discovered rather than presented
late-night current reality leaking into a procedural world
cheap objects made comfortable through arrangement
electronics as ordinary life and minor mythology
a safe pause before descending into the cramped city

hardInvariants.rule: Spawn stands on structurally safe elevated fabric with a clear capsule, generous edge margin, and immediate controller-proven movement.
One real-broadcast-capable television or monitor is the social focus, supported plausibly and visible from multiple seats.
At least two believable seating opportunities and one small shared surface create a place to stay, not merely pass through.
At least three life props imply very recent occupancy: drink, ash/snack, paper, clothing, tool, keys, or similar.
Cool moving screen light and at least one warmer practical light overlap without flattening the roof into uniform illumination.
A fictionalized giant vacuum-tube structure on a nearby building is visible from the refuge and acts as the first navigational memory.
Mechanical or communications hardware makes the location unambiguously a working rooftop.
A connector toward stairs, fire escape, hatch, door, bridge, or equivalent city circulation remains visually and physically unobstructed.
Prefer an elevated enclave with taller or comparable city mass nearby; strongly penalize isolated local maxima and exposed summit roofs.
The arrival space offers at least three controller-valid movement headings before the player is forced into a single corridor.
The location should reveal or plausibly connect to both descent and lateral continuation: stairs, fire escape, bridge, hatch, door, landing, or adjacent roof fabric.
Nearby taller masses, parapets, machinery, and layered sightlines make the player feel inside the city rather than above it.
The refuge is partially sheltered and compressed while retaining enough open sky and skyline visibility to read unmistakably as elevated exterior space.

rules: first glance sees either TV glow or vacuum-tube silhouette
at least three physically valid headings from the arrival neighborhood
one route reads as descent into the city
one route can continue laterally or remain elevated when fabric permits
furniture and utilities never collapse the route fan into a single-file exit

compositionSlots.relationship: supports primary-tv when that variant requires a surface; otherwise acts as the refuge shared surface
mostly faces primary-tv or shared surface

microstories.story: Someone has been sitting alone with the news and one slow drink.
The television or its power arrangement has recently been repaired while still in use.
Two people share the roof after work; they are absent now, but only barely.
Rain protection has been improvised around the valuable electronics and seats.
The refuge doubles as a casual listening/watch station without becoming a surveillance room.
A small social night rather than a workstation.
The skyline matters as much as the television.

antiRepeat: do not reuse exact TV+support+primary-seat tuple on consecutive world seeds when alternatives exist
expand family variety before exact asset repeat
vary microstory independently from roof utility mix
allow furniture orientation jitter only inside semantic relationships

contents: official live media embed if available

mediaIntent.fallback: dark glass / subtle static / NO SIGNAL

semanticRequirements: stable location id independent of the chosen host building/entity
host entity and space ids recorded as binding context, not identity
controller-proven spawn capsule and route fan before play
local-peak rejection and nested-city context scoring
external media lifecycle separate from world identity
successTest: Across seeds, the player should wake in visibly different elevated enclaves that still read as the same remembered refuge. The spawn must feel embedded in the city, not displayed on its summit: nearby mass, protected footing, television/refuge identity, and several meaningful navigation choices survive even when exact host roof, furniture, utilities, and routes change.
identity: A singular player-spawn location: a lived-in elevated roof-level enclave embedded inside the city mass, not perched on the city's highest exposed roof. It is a private late-night refuge with television glow, recent human presence, improvised comfort, working roof infrastructure, and several legible ways to move laterally, vertically, and down into the maze.

placementGuarantee.rule: Singularity guarantees this location identity and spawn role, not a special building, prefab, or fixed coordinate.

preferred: roof-level or elevated exterior fabric above the immediate street layer
nested among taller or comparable neighboring masses rather than crowning the skyline
protected arrival zone with meaningful standing surface around the player capsule
multiple independent movement headings before the player commits to a route
at least one legible descent toward the street maze
lateral continuation potential through roof, bridge, fire-escape, stair, hatch, door, or landing systems
several sightlines into different city layers so orientation begins immediately
partial shelter and visual compression from nearby walls, machinery, parapets, or taller buildings
enough open sky to read as elevated without feeling exposed on a summit
stronglyRejected: highest isolated roof in the local neighborhood
flat exposed peak with empty horizon on every side
spawn capsule close to an unprotected drop
street-level plaza masquerading as the authored spawn
special spawn-only geometry that bypasses normal fabric authority
spatialFingerprint.selectionDoctrine: Choose the best existing fabric space. Do not distort the city to make the spawn fit.
